findings.title: Accidental git submodule added at repo root
findings.body: The PR adds a new git submodule `sentry-repo` pinned to the base commit a5d2909. This appears to be an accidental artifact of a local checkout (the PR description even says "Test 3"), and if merged it would add a nested copy of the repository as a submodule, breaking clean clones and confusing CI/tooling. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Substring match treats "!event.type:error" as an error-focused query
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query does a naive substring check `if "event.type:error" in query`. A query like "!event.type:error" (exclude errors) or "(event.type:transaction) AND !event.type:error" also contains that substring, so it returns True. Combined with the allowlist check, count() in such queries will be silently transformed to sum(sample_weight) on the discover dataset even though the query matches non-error events, which either produces wrong counts or breaks because sample_weight doesn't exist for those rows. The query string should be parsed (or at minimum checked for negation) rather than substring-matched.

findings.title: Cache key built with Python hash() is unstable and collision-prone
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's hash() is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so every web worker computes a different key for the same project set, making the 60-second cache largely ineffective across the fleet and causing cache entries to be orphaned. Worse, hash collisions between two different project sets would cause one set's eligibility decision to be applied to the other, flipping upsampling on/off incorrectly. Use a deterministic key such as a comma-joined sorted id list or a hash from hashlib.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility checked against outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: Inside _get_event_stats, the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` rather than the `scoped_dataset` argument that is actually queried. In the dashboard-widget discover-split path, scoped_dataset is `discover` (with an errors-only query) while the outer dataset may be metrics_performance/metrics_enhanced_performance, so the transform decision is made for the wrong dataset: the errors split query never gets upsampled, and conversely a transformation decision valid for the outer dataset could be applied to a different scoped dataset. Pass scoped_dataset to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects.

findings.title: Eligibility cache has no isolation; tests and allowlist changes observe stale results
findings.body: The 60s cache keyed by (org, project set) is never invalidated when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes (invalidate_upsampling_cache exists but nothing calls it), so flipping the allowlist takes up to 60s to take effect with no code path wiring the invalidation. Additionally, tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py runs multiple tests against the same org+project set with different mocked allowlists; the first test's cached True result can leak into later tests (e.g. the partial-allowlist test expecting count==1 would get the upsampled 10) if the cache is not cleared between tests, making the suite order-dependent. Tests should clear the cache in setUp, and the option-change path should call the invalidation hook.

findings.title: Sample-rate helper swallows errors, drops valid rate 0, and runs for every stored event
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps dict .get() chains in bare try/except Exception (which cannot raise for the normal case but will silently mask real problems), and uses `if client_sample_rate:` so a legitimate client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored. More importantly, it is invoked unconditionally in Factories.store_event for every event stored in every test, mutating normalized_data['sample_rate'] globally — a hidden side effect that can change event processing behavior in unrelated tests that happen to include an error_sampling context. Consider gating it and using explicit None checks instead of truthiness and broad excepts.

findings.title: Empty project list returns False, disabling upsampling for org-wide queries
findings.body: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled returns False when project_ids is empty. Queries that target all projects in an organization (no explicit project filter) can legitimately have project_ids resolved before this call, but if snuba_params.project_ids is ever empty for an org-wide query the upsampling silently never applies with no indication why. Worth confirming the intended behavior for the all-projects case and documenting/testing it.
